citation: Ferreira, S. and Gunay, B. (2024), Building Feature Characterization Tool, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.11581431
description: The Building Feature Characterization Tool is a web application that infers building characteristics from measured heating and cooling loads, to find retrofit opportunities across large building portfolios. It was developed by Shane Ferreira and Burak Gunay at Carleton University, Ottawa, and published on Zenodo on 14 June 2024. It uses an inverse surrogate model: artificial neural networks trained on EnergyPlus simulations map load patterns back to building features, and the tool combines these with benchmarking and clustering modules so managers can screen many buildings quickly. Coverage: buildings with metered heating and cooling data; the training simulations define which building types it suits. Access: a zip of the source repository on Zenodo; its file listing shows Python modules for the neural network, benchmarks, clustering and energy calculations. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a research tool with a single release; predictions are only as good as the simulation set behind the networks. Simulation uses are portfolio-scale retrofit screening and model calibration for building energy planning. Related records: besos and EnergyPlus.
inputs: Measured heating and cooling load data of buildings
name: Building Feature Characterization Tool
outputs: Predicted building characteristics (envelope and system features)
